title: Marked simplex and spine extension inclusions
statement:
Use marked simplicial sets, sharp marking, and marked coanodyne maps from [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne]. For $n\geq1$, let $I^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ be the simplicial spine, the union of the consecutive edges $\Delta^{\{i-1,i\}}$ for $1\leq i\leq n$, and put $I^0=\Delta^0$. The two marked inclusions
$$\{0\}^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\sharp,\qquad (I^n)^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\sharp$$
are marked coanodyne for every $n\geq0$. Consequently, if a marked map $q:X\to Y$ has the right lifting property against marked coanodyne maps, either inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ has the following relative parameter extension property: for any monomorphism $T\hookrightarrow T'$ of simplicial sets, marked maps from $((\Delta^n)^\sharp\times T^\flat)\amalg_{U\times T^\flat}(U\times(T')^\flat)$ to $X$ over a prescribed marked map $(\Delta^n)^\sharp\times(T')^\flat\to Y$ extend to $(\Delta^n)^\sharp\times(T')^\flat$. The parameter may be empty and its prescribed data may be an entire boundary, not just a horn.

source.place: Agent combinatorial consequence of HTT Definition 3.1.1.1 (opposite marked horn and triangle generators), with the relative parameter clause given by Proposition 3.1.2.3 under opposite reversal. The explicit subset/horn filtration is recorded in the second-reading report; Corollary 2.3.2.5 is an exponentiation result and is not cited as a spine-filtration theorem. Read directly in the IAS PDF. No Stacks tag states this marked assertion.
